title: One Nuke on Kaliningrad: What If NATO Cut It Off?
description:
What would a Russian nuclear warning shot in Kaliningrad look like if NATO cut off the Suwalki gap?

A 5-kiloton air burst on Russian soil, 3 minutes after the launch, and 13 days of pressure that lead to it: this simulation follows the crisis day by day, then the blast rings and the day after.

Six thirteen in the evening, Kaliningrad. One Iskander missile flies 98 kilometres and one nuclear weapon bursts over open ground inside Russia itself. Why would Russia fire at its own land, and what does NATO do in the hour after? Before the simulation we look at what is real: the 65 km Suwalki gap, Kaliningrad's missiles and its only supply lines, and the 2022 rail ban and the Berlin blockade.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. The cut-off, the missile, the yield and the target are fictional design choices built from published models, not predictions. NATO denies any plan to isolate the enclave.
